'''David Destefanis''' won the [[2000 Rome Grand Slam]]<ref name="gs00" /> and the [[2000 Chandrila Regionals]].<ref name="dc00fin" /> He also finished fifth at the [[2014 European Championship Reset Beta]].<ref name="pc" /> In March 2004, as "DDM", he was one of the two winners of the ''[[Forfeit Zero]]'' 100th-comic contest; the comic's character David De Master, in a Napoleonic bicorne, was created for him.<ref name="fz-contest">[https://comic.forfeitzero.com/text/20040319.txt "Double Your Pleasure"], news post by Brian Sabotta (ben_ethus), ''Forfeit Zero'' (19 March 2004).</ref>

On the Players Committee forum, as DDM, his signature in captures of June and July 2004 read "SWCCGPC Webgroup Member".<ref name="pcf-3296-46224">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46224#46224 Ratings - see PC announcement], David Destefanis, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625214243/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46459%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-3180-45018">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=45018#45018 SWCCG worlds and more], David Destefanis, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (19 April 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040709185410/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=45251%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In April 2004 he wrote that he lived in Italy and had travelled to the World Championships in 1998, with all expenses paid, and in 2000, with the trip paid, but not in 2001 or 2003; in the same post he proposed area-based online tournaments on CardTable, for example European, East USA and West USA events with a final between the winners.<ref name="pcf-3180-45018" /> In May 2004 he was the contact for the 2004 Chandrila State Championship, planned for 13 June 2004 in Rome, and wrote that the event had drawn 18 players in 2003 and 14 in 2002.<ref name="pcf-3364-46870">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46870#46870 Chandrila States (Italy)], David Destefanis, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (28 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041031011229/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46870%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> According to his forum signature (captured December 2004), he was an "SWCCG European Finalist" with Massassi Base Operations.<ref name="pcf-3422-47301">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=47301#47301 Alternate Virtual Card Format?!], David Destefanis, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (8 June 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041225122828/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=47262%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

== Card credits ==
David Destefanis is credited on [[Players Committee]] [[Virtual cards]] with the original concept of two cards.<ref name="labels">[https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/src/gemp-swccg-cards/src/main/resources/card_labels.json card_labels.json] in billbisco/swccg-gemp (commit 0bc4377d9): the printed labels of every Players Committee Virtual card, transcribed from the PC's card images. Field definitions: [https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/docs/card_labels.md docs/card_labels.md].</ref> The printed concept credit names the tournament or award with the concept: a [[DeckTech]] contest ("DeckTech Contest Winner 04") on •The Time For Our Attack Has Come (V) ([[Virtual Block 3]]). The credited cards were printed in [[Virtual Block 3]] (2009) and [[Virtual Set 10]] (2019), so the credited cards span 2009–2019. The full list of people credited on Virtual cards is at [[Card Credits#David Destefanis|Card Credits]].

''Year'' is the set's release date (Virtual Sets) or the date its official text took effect (Virtual Blocks), as given in the set's article. Alternate-image (AI, ALT) and back faces are counted as separate cards, as on [[Card Credits]].
